title: Identify purpose, tone and main idea in the quiet-hour report
instructions: Read the complete passage. Distinguish the central message, the writer's purpose and the writer's tone. Test each answer against the whole passage rather than one detail. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: A limited quiet period has shown promise for some readers, while the library continues to test and adapt it for different visitors.
Every public library should remain completely silent throughout the weekend.
The main reason book loans increased was that school examinations were approaching.
Picture cards are the most effective way to control children's behaviour in libraries.

choice_rationales.A: This covers the promising observations, the limited scope and the continuing adjustments developed across the passage.
choice_rationales.B: The quiet period affects one room for one hour, and the writer does not recommend silence throughout every library.
choice_rationales.C: Examinations are presented as a limitation on interpretation, not as a proven cause of the increase.
choice_rationales.D: Picture cards are one practical response, not the passage's central message.

parts.hint: Choose the option that still fits paragraphs 1, 3, 4 and 5.
parts.correct_explanation: The passage presents encouraging early evidence while stressing that the trial is limited, inclusive adjustments are needed and further comparison will follow.

parts.prompt: What is the writer's main purpose in this passage?

options.text: To entertain readers with a humorous account of badly behaved library visitors.
To persuade every family to avoid the library on Saturday mornings.
To evaluate an early library trial by explaining its design, results, limitations and response to concerns.
To provide instructions for constructing a new upstairs reading room.

choice_rationales.A: The report is factual and measured rather than humorous, and it does not focus on misconduct.
choice_rationales.B: The library is trying to serve different visitors and invites further feedback; it does not urge families to stay away.
choice_rationales.C: The passage explains how the trial works, examines observations and limitations, and describes adjustments before reaching a provisional judgment.
choice_rationales.D: The room already exists, and no construction process is described.

parts.hint: Complete this sentence with the most precise verb: the writer aims to ___ the trial.
parts.correct_explanation: By presenting design, evidence, concerns, changes and next steps, the writer evaluates the trial rather than merely announcing or promoting it.

parts.prompt: Which description best captures the writer's tone towards the Quiet First Hour?

options.text: Triumphant and certain
Cautiously positive and measured
Mocking and dismissive
Alarmed and hostile

choice_rationales.A: The writer calls the figures encouraging but repeatedly preserves uncertainty and scope.
choice_rationales.B: Positive observations are balanced with limitations, concerns and the need for more evidence.
choice_rationales.C: Neither the visitors nor the experiment are ridiculed.
choice_rationales.D: The writer describes manageable concerns without expressing alarm or hostility.

parts.hint: Combine the positive word used in paragraph 4 with the qualification that follows it.
parts.correct_explanation: The language recognises encouraging results while qualifying them with although, still and the need for a longer comparison.

parts.prompt: What does the description that newcomers 'tended to soften their footsteps without being reminded' contribute to the passage?

options.text: It proves that all visitors understood every written rule before entering.
It provides an observed detail suggesting that the atmosphere itself encouraged quieter behaviour.
It shows that staff punished newcomers who made noise.
It establishes that borrowing books depends on walking quietly.

choice_rationales.A: The detail concerns behaviour and does not show what every visitor read or understood.
choice_rationales.B: The observation supports the description of the room's atmosphere without making an absolute causal claim.
choice_rationales.C: The newcomers changed their behaviour without a reminder; no punishment is described.
choice_rationales.D: The passage reports both book loans and quieter movement but does not make one a condition of the other.

parts.hint: Decide whether the sentence is an observation, a rule, a punishment or a proven cause.
parts.correct_explanation: The detail helps readers picture a quiet atmosphere that influenced behaviour, while remaining a limited observation rather than proof.

parts.prompt: Select the two details that most directly support the passage's balanced main idea.

options.text: Use of the room and book loans increased over the first six Saturdays.
The floor signs used three languages.
The later Saturdays occurred near examinations, and the survey included people who chose to use the room.
The reading room was located upstairs.
The library doors opened before some waiting visitors entered.

choice_rationales.A: The increases provide the main positive evidence that the trial attracted readers.
choice_rationales.B: The languages are a useful implementation detail but do not establish the trial's overall promise and uncertainty.
choice_rationales.C: These limitations explain why the encouraging figures require further testing.
choice_rationales.D: Location identifies the room but does not support the central evaluation.
choice_rationales.E: This paraphrases a minor scene without representing the passage's main balance.

parts.hint: Choose one detail showing promise and one detail limiting the conclusion.
parts.correct_explanation: The increased use supplies encouraging evidence, while examination timing and self-selection prevent a conclusive judgment.

parts.prompt: What is the main role of the final paragraph?

options.text: It introduces an unrelated programme that will replace the quiet hour.
It repeats the opening rules without adding any judgment.
It gives a final guarantee that the arrangement suits every visitor.
It states the next evidence to collect and closes with a qualified assessment of the trial.

choice_rationales.A: The extended trial continues the same initiative.
choice_rationales.B: The paragraph adds future comparison, broader feedback and a provisional conclusion.
choice_rationales.C: The final sentence explicitly rejects a universal conclusion.
choice_rationales.D: The future data and Anwar's qualified judgment complete the report's evaluation.

parts.hint: Look for both a future action and the degree of certainty in the closing sentence.
parts.correct_explanation: The paragraph explains how the library will strengthen its evidence and ends with a proportionate, qualified judgment.
